provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Surah Al - Ikhlas
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite Surah Al - Ikhlas.
The pupils should be able to explain the meaning of Surah Al - Ikhlas.

Introduction:
Today we will learn Surah Al - Ikhlas. We have learned many short surahs before.

Content:
Surah Al - Ikhlas means the purity of faith. It teaches that Allah is one. Allah has no partner. Allah does not give birth nor was Allah born. No one is like Allah. We recite this surah to remember Allah is one.

Class activity:
The pupils will recite Surah Al - Ikhlas together in lines.

Evaluation questions:
What is the meaning of Surah Al - Ikhlas?
How many verses are in Surah Al - Ikhlas?
What does Surah Al - Ikhlas teach about Allah?

Summary:
Surah Al - Ikhlas teaches us that Allah is one and has no partners.

topics.title: Surah Al - Falaq and An - Nas
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite Surah Al - Falaq and An - Nas.
The pupils should be able to explain why we seek Allah's protection.

Introduction:
Today we will learn two important surahs for protection. We have learned how to praise Allah with Surah Al - Ikhlas.

Content:
Surah Al - Falaq means the dawn. It teaches us to seek protection from Allah from harm. Surah An - Nas means people. It teaches us to seek protection from Allah from the evil of people who may harm us. We recite these surahs for safety.

Class activity:
The pupils will practice reciting Surah Al - Falaq and An - Nas after the teacher.

Evaluation questions:
What does Surah Al - Falaq mean?
What does Surah An - Nas mean?
Why do we recite these two surahs?

Summary:
Surah Al - Falaq and An - Nas teach us to seek Allah's protection from harm.

topics.title: Salah in congregation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain the importance of praying together.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate proper lines for congregational prayer.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about praying in congregation. We know how to pray alone five times a day.

Content:
Praying in congregation means praying together with other Muslims. It brings unity among Muslims. We stand in straight lines with no gaps. The imam stands in front. We follow the imam's movements. This is called jama'ah. It is better to pray in congregation than alone.

Class activity:
The pupils will practice forming straight lines for prayer and following the imam.

Evaluation questions:
What is congregational prayer called?
Who stands in front during congregational prayer?
Why is praying together important?

Summary:
Praying in congregation brings unity and is better than praying alone.

topics.title: Fasting in Ramadan
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why Muslims fast in Ramadan.
The pupils should be able to list benefits of fasting.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about fasting in Ramadan. We have learned about the five pillars of Islam.

Content:
Fasting in Ramadan is one of the five pillars of Islam. We do not eat or drink from dawn to sunset. We fast to learn self - control. We learn to be patient with hunger. We also feel poor people who have no food. Fasting teaches us to be good Muslims.

Class activity:
The pupils will share what they do during Ramadan to help others.

Evaluation questions:
What are the hours for fasting in Ramadan?
Why do Muslims fast in Ramadan?
What does fasting teach us?

Summary:
Fasting teaches self - control and helps us understand the poor.

topics.title: The Prophet's honesty
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall the Prophet's nickname Al - Amin.
The pupils should be able to explain how to be trustworthy like the Prophet.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about the Prophet Muhammad's honesty. We know the Prophet is our role model.

Content:
The Prophet Muhammad was called Al - Amin which means the trustworthy. Even before Islam, people trusted him with their money and secrets. He was honest in everything he did. He never told a lie. We should be like him by always telling the truth and keeping our promises.

Class activity:
The pupils will role - play situations where they can show honesty.

Evaluation questions:
What was the Prophet's nickname?
Give one example of the Prophet's honesty.
How can you be like the Prophet in your daily life?

Summary:
The Prophet was called Al - Amin because he was always honest and trustworthy.

topics.title: Cleanliness is faith
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain the concept of taharah.
The pupils should be able to list clean habits Muslims should have.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about cleanliness in Islam. We know that Allah loves cleanliness.

Content:
Cleanliness in Arabic is called taharah. Islam teaches us to be clean in body and clothes. We should wash our hands before eating. We should take regular baths. We should keep our homes and school clean. Being clean is part of our faith. The Prophet said cleanliness is half of faith.

Class activity:
The pupils will demonstrate proper handwashing before eating.

Evaluation questions:
What is the Arabic word for cleanliness?
Why is cleanliness important in Islam?
Name two clean habits Muslims should have.

Summary:
Cleanliness is part of faith and we should practice it daily.

topics.title: Good manners
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the proper Islamic greeting.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate how to greet others properly.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about good Islamic manners. We know that Islam teaches us to be good to others.

Content:
The proper Islamic greeting is Assalamu Alaikum which means peace be upon you. When we greet others, we should say it with a smile. We should greet our parents, teachers, and friends. When someone greets us, we should reply with Wa Alaikumus Salam. This shows good manners and respect.

Class activity:
The pupils will practice greeting each other with Assalamu Alaikum and the proper response.

Evaluation questions:
What is the proper Islamic greeting?
How should we reply when someone greets us?
Why is greeting important in Islam?

Summary:
Greeting with Assalamu Alaikum is an important sunnah of the Prophet.

topics.title: Respect for elders
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how to show respect to parents and teachers.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate polite speech when speaking to elders.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about respecting elders. We know that Islam teaches us to be respectful to our parents and teachers.

Content:
Respect for elders is very important in Islam. We should speak politely to our parents and teachers. We should use words like please and thank you. We should listen when they speak. We should not shout at them. We should help our parents with housework. These actions show our respect and good manners.

Class activity:
The pupils will role - play conversations with parents and teachers using polite speech.

Evaluation questions:
How should we speak to our elders?
Name two ways to show respect to parents.
Why is respecting elders important in Islam?

Summary:
We should always show respect to our parents and teachers with polite speech and actions.

topics.title: Brotherhood in Islam
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain the concept of Muslim brotherhood.
The pupils should be able to list ways to show peace to all Muslims.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about brotherhood in Islam. We know that all Muslims are part of one big family.

Content:
All Muslims are brothers and sisters in Islam. This means we should love and help each other. We should not fight or argue with other Muslims. We should share what we have with those in need. We should visit sick Muslims. We should forgive each other. This brotherhood makes the Muslim community strong and united.

Class activity:
The pupils will discuss ways they can help a new student in their class.

Evaluation questions:
What does Muslim brotherhood teach us?
How can we show love to other Muslims?
Why is Muslim brotherhood important?

Summary:
Muslim brotherhood teaches us to love and help all Muslims like family.

topics.title: Revision and recitation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite all surahs learned this term.
The pupils should be able to explain the main lessons from each surah.

Introduction:
Today we will revise what we learned this term. We have studied many important surahs and topics.

Content:
We will recite Surah Al - Ikhlas, Al - Falaq, and An - Nas together. We will remember what each surah teaches. We will review the importance of congregational prayer, fasting in Ramadan, the Prophet's honesty, cleanliness, good manners, respect for elders, and Muslim brotherhood. These are all important lessons for good Muslims.

Class activity:
The pupils will take turns reciting the surahs and explaining their meanings.

Evaluation questions:
What does Surah Al - Ikhlas teach?
Why is fasting important in Ramadan?
How do we show respect to our elders?
What is the proper Islamic greeting?

Summary:
We have learned many important lessons this term that help us become good Muslims.
